questions.question: What is the definition of climate?
options: The daily changes in wind speed and temperature in a local area.
The average weather conditions for a particular location over a long period of time.
The atmospheric pressure and rainfall recorded over a single week.
The seasonal differences in daylight hours across the planet.

questions.question: What is causing global warming and climate change?
options: Emissions of greenhouse gases from human activities.
An increase in volcanic activity on the ocean floor.
Natural changes in the distance between the Earth and the Sun.
A gradual decrease in the Earth's atmospheric pressure.

questions.question: What does climate change include?
options: A decrease in the strength of ocean tides globally.
An increase in the frequency of extreme weather events such as droughts, storms and floods.
A steady decrease in the number of active volcanoes.
An increase in the Earth's gravitational pull.

questions.question: What must we do to successfully limit climate change?
options: Rely solely on plants to naturally absorb all excess carbon without changing our behavior.
We all need to work together to reduce emissions of greenhouse gases to limit climate change.
Stop all agricultural activity and food production worldwide.
Wait for future technologies to completely replace the atmosphere.

questions.question: Which of the following lists the factors that add to the carbon footprint of food?
options: Only the distance food is transported from the farm to the shop.
Land-use change, farming, processing, transport, retail and packaging.
Only the materials used to package the final product.
The energy used by the consumer to cook the food at home.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the carbon footprints of meat and plant-based food products?
options: Meat and plant-based products have different carbon footprints.
They have the exact same carbon footprint because both are agricultural products.
Plant-based products always have a higher carbon footprint than meat.
Neither meat nor plant-based products have a carbon footprint.

questions.question: When is food production considered to be more sustainable?
options: When it maximizes short-term crop yields regardless of soil erosion.
When it uses as much fresh water and artificial fertilizer as possible.
When it has a smaller, negative impact on the environment.
When it relies entirely on air freight for international distribution.

questions.question: How can changes in our diet and a reduction in food waste help us eat more sustainably?
options: By increasing our reliance on heavily packaged and processed foods.
By lowering greenhouse gas emissions.
By forcing all food to be grown indoors using artificial light.
By encouraging the consumption of out-of-season imported crops.

questions.question: What do temperature data show about the Earth's average surface temperature over the last century or so?
options: An unusual, rapid increase in the Earth's average surface temperature.
A steady and continuous cooling trend across all continents.
No change at all compared to historical averages.
A slow, predictable decrease in temperature.

questions.question: What is the name given to the recent increase in the Earth's average surface temperature?
options: The ozone effect.
Global warming.
Thermal convection.
Atmospheric pressure.

questions.question: What relationship is shown between temperature data and greenhouse gas emissions data?
options: There is a correlation between data showing increasing temperature and data showing increasing greenhouse gas emissions.
There is no relationship or pattern between the two sets of data.
The data show that rising temperatures cause greenhouse gas emissions to drop.
The data show that greenhouse gas emissions decrease as temperatures rise.

questions.question: What do most scientists agree is the cause of global warming?
options: An increase in solar radiation due to changes in the Sun's core.
Emissions from human activities are increasing the greenhouse effect, causing global warming.
Natural cycles of heat rising from the Earth's mantle.
A decrease in the overall thickness of the Earth's atmosphere.

questions.question: How can thermal insulators help to make a building more energy-efficient?
options: They generate heat energy to warm the rooms automatically.
Thermal insulators can reduce the energy needed to heat a building.
They allow heat to escape more quickly during cold weather.
They convert solar energy directly into usable electricity.

questions.question: What is the benefit of using thermostats in a building's heating system?
options: They increase the rate of heat transfer through the walls.
They generate renewable energy to power home appliances.
Thermostats can control temperature automatically in different rooms and help reduce unnecessary heating.
They prevent any fresh air from entering the building.

questions.question: Why do renewable resources not run out?
options: They are stored in infinite quantities deep inside the Earth.
They are replenished faster than they are used up.
They are completely indestructible and cannot be destroyed.
They are synthetic materials manufactured in large factories.

questions.question: Under what condition is a resource like wood considered renewable?
options: Some resources, such as wood, are only renewable if they are used sustainably.
Wood is always renewable, no matter how quickly we chop down forests.
Wood is only renewable if it is imported from tropical regions.
Wood is never renewable because trees take too long to grow.

questions.question: Which statement is true regarding sustainable transport?
options: We cannot have sustainable transport that uses petrol or diesel fuel.
Petrol and diesel vehicles are sustainable as long as they have modern filters.
Only public transport using diesel engines is considered sustainable.
Any vehicle is sustainable if it travels at a constant speed.

questions.question: What is the role of the natural greenhouse effect on Earth?
options: It causes extreme weather events like hurricanes to happen daily.
A natural greenhouse effect maintains optimal temperature range for life on Earth.
It blocks all heat from the Sun from reaching the planet's surface.
It causes the oceans to boil away over time.

questions.question: How are human activities affecting the Earth's greenhouse effect?
options: Human activities are decreasing the amount of greenhouse gases, cooling the planet.
Human activities are increasing the amount of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere, increasing the greenhouse effect.
Human activities have absolutely no effect on the natural greenhouse effect.
Human activities are causing the greenhouse gases to escape into space.

questions.question: What actions can we take to minimise the amount of waste we produce?
options: Incinerate, bury, and discard.
Reuse, reduce, recycle is what we can do to minimise waste.
Export, accumulate, and replace.
Landfill, burn, and export.
